editorial.headline: Gas and Discharge Lamps: Open Nationally, Blocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 27402 covers the manufacture of gas and discharge lamps; nationally it is foreign-open, but Bali blocks PMA registration under its risk-class moratorium.
editorial.body:
KBLI 27402 is a manufacturing classification for gas and discharge lamps. The record defines the activity as the making of various gas and discharge lamps, including neon, helium, argon, sodium, and mercury lamps, as well as electric lamps used for insect traps. Its center of gravity is therefore industrial production, not retailing, installation, or lighting consultancy. A company using this code should be able to point to the actual manufacture of these lamp types as the activity being registered.

The scale picture is broad. The record opens this activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar enterprises, so the classification is not reserved only for large factories. It can describe a small producer as well as a larger manufacturing operation, provided the activity remains within the recorded scope: making gas and discharge lamps and the included electric insect-trap lamps. That breadth matters because the KBLI code is about the nature of the activity first, while the business scale sits alongside it as a registration dimension.

Nationally, the foreign-investment signal is clear. The record marks the PMA status as TERBUKA and gives a pma_max_asing of 100, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. In plain English, the national record treats this activity as open to foreign ownership up to 100%. There is no lower foreign-share ceiling in the slim record, and no special national condition stated here beyond that open status and source reference.

Bali is the decisive exception. The same record marks l4_bali_blocked as true and gives the reason as: "OSS risk at scale Besar is Rendah/Menengah-Rendah on every scope → blocked by Bali moratorium 13 May 2026". It also states the Bali moratorium rule: "Bali province blocks ALL Low + Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA (island-wide, permanent)". So the honest reading is not that KBLI 27402 is difficult, ambiguous, or merely capped in Bali. It is nationally open to PMA, yet blocked for PMA registration in Bali under the Bali-side risk-class moratorium recorded here.
editorial.pullQuote: KBLI 27402 is nationally open to 100% foreign ownership, yet blocked for PMA registration in Bali under the recorded risk-class moratorium.
